newsitem.title: MOROCCO: MOROCCO'S BOURSE HEADS HIGHER FOR SECOND DAY.
newsitem.headline: MOROCCO'S BOURSE HEADS HIGHER FOR SECOND DAY.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange on Wednesday closed 0.24 percent higher, pursuing an upward trend after a slight drop at the start of the week, a trader said.
The all-share index closed at 689.75 points, from 688.10 points on Tuesday.
"The market index continued on Wednesday its rising trend pushed up the market blue chips, including the Societe Nationale d'Investissement," a Casablanca-based stockbroker said.
The index has risen 53.89 percent since the beginning of 1997, the stockbrocker said.
But a mutual fund analyst said stock prices were overpriced and did not reflect the real activity and growth of the market.
"There is too much speculation on the Casablanca bourse. It led to an artificial surge of share prices...We expect the market index to go down and stabilise soon," the analyst said.
Societe Nationale d'Investissment conglomerate, which has diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, jumped 21 dirhams to close at 754 dirhams.
The rise followed its release on Wednesday of its 1996 consolidated results, showing a net profit of 417 million dirhams ($44.3 million), up 10.3 percent over 1995.

"SNI, which is one of the stock market most liquid stocks, showed a performance of 30.9 percent with 2.0 billion dirhams worth of transactions in 1996," the group's chairman M'Fadel Lahlou told Reuters.
Its turnover rose by 16 percent to 4.4 billion dirhams in 1996 from 3.8 billion dirhams in 1995, Lahlou said.
ONA Group, the country's largest private conglomerate, gained 16 dirhams to close at 840 dirhams.

The group, which holds stakes in more than 80 companies and has the largest market capitalisation of 14.4 billion dirhams, announced last week a net profit of 878.7 million dirhams in 1996, up from 602.6 million dirhams in 1995.
In the banking sector, blue chip Wafabank rose 18 dirhams to 860.
The bank announced that the board of directors approved the merger-absorption of Spanish Uniban bank. Uniban is expected to be de-listed from the bourse on June 2, 1997, officials said.
Wafabank is expected to increase its capital by 49.2 million dirhams ($5.34 million).
Total traded volume rose to more than 126 million dirhams from more than 106 million dirhams on Tuesday.

It was divided into 86.7 million dirhams in shares and 2.1 million dirhams in privatisation bonds traded on the official market. The remaining 37.3 million dirhams were traded in shares on the over the counter market, officials said.
